lead_headline: Council Places Moratorium on Large Data Center Applications, Advances to First Reading

type_specific.meeting_summary: The Arvada City Council, meeting without Mayor Simpson (excused), approved three proclamations, passed several consent and resolution items, and advanced five ordinances to first reading — including a moratorium on large data center applications. The council also voted to have an independent third party conduct a pending ethics hearing involving Council Member Davis, and heard public comment on topics ranging from park maintenance and short-term rentals to Amendment 83 and Proposition 123 affordable housing procedures.

tonight_at_a_glance.synopsis: Council approved five first-reading ordinances including a data center moratorium and two annexations, voted 4–1 to send a council ethics matter to a third-party hearing officer, and heard extensive public comment on parks, short-term rentals, and a proposed state constitutional amendment on hunting.
highlights: Data center moratorium ordinance advanced to first reading; public hearing set for October 6
Two water treatment plant annexation ordinances and related rezoning advanced to first reading
Ordinance amending residential land use table advanced to first reading
Ethics hearing for Council Member Davis referred to independent third-party hearing officer (4–1)
Consent agenda passed 6–0: flood control IGA amendment, Gold Strike Park construction contract, and animal shelter IGA update
